questions.q: What real feedback mechanism does an end user have on a Published article?
options: Feedback can only be submitted by the article's original author
A Helpful / Not Helpful control, tracked and aggregated into a visible rating for that article
There is no real feedback mechanism on Published articles
End users can only provide feedback by opening a new Incident
questions.explain: Helpful / Not Helpful responses aggregate into a real, visible signal a Knowledge manager can act on.

questions.q: Why does a well-implemented instance retire an outdated article instead of deleting it?
options: Retiring is only available for articles that never received any feedback
Deleting and retiring have exactly the same effect on the record
Retiring removes it from active search while preserving its full history; deleting destroys that audit trail entirely
Retired articles remain visible in search results, unlike deleted ones
questions.explain: Retired is a distinct Workflow state that keeps the article's author, review, and feedback history intact while taking it out of active search.

questions.q: What does a falling Helpful ratio tell a Knowledge manager?
options: That the article, as written, is not solving the problem it claims to solve, and likely needs revision
Nothing useful — Helpful ratios have no real implementation purpose
That the article's Workflow state is automatically set to Published
That the article should be immediately retired with no review
questions.explain: A falling Helpful ratio is a real signal that should trigger pulling the article back into Draft for revision.

questions.q: What does a periodic review cadence typically check for?
options: Articles that have gone 12 months or more without being updated, regardless of whether they've received negative feedback yet
Whether an article's Category field has ever been changed
Only articles with zero Helpful votes
Only articles that have already been Retired
questions.explain: A scheduled check flags articles nobody has touched in a year, since unverified content may no longer be accurate even without negative feedback yet.

questions.q: How do Problem Management's Known Error articles relate to this lifecycle?
options: Known Error articles can never be retired, even after the underlying problem is fixed
They are stored as kb_knowledge records and follow the same Draft, Review, Published, and eventual Retired lifecycle as any other article
Known Error articles are stored in a completely separate table with no Workflow state
Known Error articles skip the approval workflow entirely
questions.explain: Known Error articles are real kb_knowledge records and should be retired once the underlying problem is permanently fixed and the workaround is no longer needed.
